title: Derived constant realization commutes with derived scalar extension
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] and let $q:R\to S$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings, with induced map $\underline q:\underline R\to\underline S$ of constant ring sheaves [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], the derived constant realizations $c_R:D(R)\to D(\mathcal C,\underline R)$ and $c_S:D(S)\to D(\mathcal C,\underline S)$ [def-sfb-site-derived-constant-module-functor], derived scalar extension along $q$ and along $\underline q$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] (along $q$ on the one-object site with only the identity covering), and restriction of scalars [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. For every $M\in D(R)$ there is an isomorphism $$\kappa_M:c_R(M)\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\underline R}\underline S\xrightarrow{\sim}c_S(M\otimes^{\mathbf L}_RS)$$ in $D(\mathcal C,\underline S)$, natural in $M$, with the following properties. (1) If $K^\bullet$ is a K-flat complex of $R$-modules with flat terms representing $M$ [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], then $c_R(K^\bullet)$ (termwise constant sheaves) is a K-flat complex of $\underline R$-modules with flat terms, and $\kappa_M$ is represented by the termwise isomorphism $c_R(K^p)\otimes_{\underline R}\underline S\cong c_S(K^p\otimes_RS)$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] induced by the identity of the constant presheaves with value $K^p\otimes_RS$. (2) Under $\kappa_M$ and the identification of $c_S$ followed by restriction to $\underline R$ with $c_R$ followed by restriction to $R$, the realization $c_R$ of the scalar-extension unit $M\to M\otimes^{\mathbf L}_RS$ is the scalar-extension unit $c_R(M)\to c_R(M)\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\underline R}\underline S$. (3) For a further homomorphism $S\to T$, the isomorphisms $\kappa$ for $R\to S$, $S\to T$ and $R\to T$ are compatible with the canonical transitivity isomorphisms $(-\otimes^{\mathbf L}S)\otimes^{\mathbf L}T\cong-\otimes^{\mathbf L}T$ on both sides. No boundedness, finiteness or Noetherian hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: Establish the actual ordinary and derived restriction adjunctions before constructing their mates. The ordinary exactness and tensor adjunction follow from lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction and lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings. The sheaf derived adjunction follows by applying the coefficient theorem to the everywhere-defined homotopy derived pair. On ordinary modules use lem-weil-pbc-derived-module-scalar-adjunction. For independently chosen localization sizes, conjugate the common-size derived restriction by the canonical Localization.uniq equivalences; compare the composite factorization on cochain complexes and use localization full faithfulness to identify it with actual exact derived restriction. Naturality of both comparison maps follows by applying the adjunction Hom bijection, then naturality of the scalar unit and restriction comparison. The normalized constant-restriction comparison remains the original sheafification argument in Step 6. Ordinary restriction composition is the sectionwise identity: functoriality of constant ring sheafification identifies its scalar actions, and sectionwise extensionality proves its uniqueness.

Constant realization preserves flat modules by the local equational criterion, and flat-term K-flat complexes by its flat-preserving colimit construction. This works directly for an arbitrary site, without constructing a geometric morphism to a point site.

For an $R$-module $A$, apply [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-tensor] to the constant ring presheaf $R$ and the constant module presheaves $A,S$. Their presheaf tensor has value $A\otimes_RS$ and identity restrictions. Hence obtain $\theta_A:c_R(A)\otimes_{\underline R}\underline S\cong c_S(A\otimes_RS)$. The map is $\underline S$-linear: multiplication by a local constant $s\in S$ acts on the second tensor factor on each side, and these local equations uniquely extend by module sheafification [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-interface]. Thus this is an isomorphism in the category of $\underline S$-modules, not merely after restriction. On constant generators it sends $a\otimes s$ to $a\otimes s$, and is natural in $A$. Its naturality for $d_K^p$ makes $(\theta_{K^p})_p$ a chain isomorphism $c_R(K)\otimes_{\underline R}\underline S\cong c_S(K\otimes_RS)$; there is no totalization or interchange of infinite products here.

The normalized constant-restriction isomorphism is obtained by the module sheafification universal property; its underlying local isomorphism is checked on constant generators. The ordinary tensor comparison uses the actual sheaf tensor product and sheafification. These existing constructions remain unchanged.

For ordinary scalar extension use extension preservation of K-flat quasi-isomorphisms. For sheaf scalar extension transfer change-of-rings invariance from the actual tensor functor along the unique ordinary left-adjoint comparison. The exact-right-adjoint representative theorem identifies both canonical representative maps as isomorphisms on K-flat complexes, with independent localization sizes.

Transpose the representative square. Ordinary mate/unit compatibility, exact-square factorization and naturality of exact derived functor comparisons prove its equality. Every derived module is represented by a flat-term K-flat resolution, so this square makes its comparison invertible. Naturality transfers this to every object. The mate definition proves the unit identity directly.

Prove ordinary restriction-comparison coherence on constant generators by sheafification extensionality. Exact-square composition transports it to the derived categories. Transpose the tower identity under the composite derived adjunction. Naturality, restriction coherence and the unit equation for left-adjoint uniqueness identify both sides with the same composite unit. No successive tensor-normalization theorem or additional K-flat representative is needed.

tool_uses.why: Finite-limit preservation constructs the point geometric morphism for any small site; no integral-model lemma states this general site fact.
General ringed-topos K-flat preservation specializes to the point geometric morphism; this is a homological tool for constant realizations, not an alternative integral-model route.
Existence of unbounded flat-term K-flat representatives on the point site.
General presheaf/module sheafification tensor comparison gives the ordinary comparison with its S action.
Universal property of the induced sheafified module action ensures linearity, restriction compatibility and equality on generators.
General unbounded scalar extension and its K-flat computation on the point and the given site.
Its K-flat homotopy-subcategory localization equivalence supplies descent to all derived morphisms.
Extension and uniqueness of natural transformations through localization.
General coefficient adjunction explicitly normalizes the unit as x maps to x tensor 1; a definition or unnormalized adjunction would not suffice.
Successive scalar extension can use the original representative because its first extension remains K-flat with flat terms.
